text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on December 9 in history.
1594 - Gustavus II of Sweden born; Sweden had become the strongest power in Europe at his death in 1632.
1608 - British poet John Milton, best known for "Paradise Lost", "Paradise Regained" and "Samson Agonistes", born.
1625 - The Treaty of the Hague was signed under which England and the Netherlands agreed to subsidise Christian IV of Denmark in his campaign in Germany.
1641 - Flemish artist Anthony Van Dyck died.
1868 - W.E. Gladstone became British prime minister for the first of his four terms.
1886 - U.S. inventor Clarence Birdseye born; famous for his invention of deep-freezing foodstuffs which he apparently learned from Eskimoes in Alaska.
1905 - Richard Strauss's one-act opera "Salome" premiered in Dresden, Germany.

1909 - Actor Douglas Fairbanks Jr. born; his most famous screen roles included Rupert of Hentzau in "The Prisoner of Zenda" (1937), both twins in "The Corsican Brothers" (1941) and "Sinbad the Sailor" (1946).
1915 - Elisabeth Schwarzkopf, German opera and concert singer, born.
1916 - Film star Kirk Douglas born as Issur Danielovitch; famed for his appearances in "Spartacus" and also "Lust for Life" as the painter Van Gogh.
1917 - Turkish troops surrendered Jerusalem to British troops led by Viscount Allenby.
1929 - Australian politician Robert Hawke born; he was prime minister from 1983-1991.
1940 - The British Eighth Army launched an offensive in North Africa by attacking Sidi Barrani in Egypt.
1941 - China formally issued a declaration of war against Japan, Germany and Italy.
1958 - The John Birch Society was founded in the U.S., vowing to fight communism.
1961 - Tanganyika became independent within the Commonwealth, with Julius Nyerere as prime minister; one year later, it became a republic within the Commonwealth.
1964 - English poet Dame Edith Sitwell died.
1965 - Nikolai Podgorny replaced Anastas Mikoyan as Soviet president.
1966 - Barbados became the 122nd member of the U.N.
1967 - The Cunard liner Queen Mary docked at Long Beach, California, after her final voyage.

1985 - Former Argentine president Jorge Videla and his fellow junta member, Admiral Emilio Massera, were sentenced to life imprisonment for their part in the "dirty war" against left-wing guerrillas in which up to 9,000 people disappeared.
1987 - The first riots of the intifada, or Palestinian uprising, erupted on the Gaza Strip.
1990 - Lech Walesa, former leader of of the trade union Solidarity, won a landslide victory in the Polish presidential election.
1992 - U.S. Marines stormed into Mogadishu, spearheading an international effort to overcome one of the worst famines this century.
1992 - The separation of the Prince and Princess of Wales was announced.
1993 - Gabon's Omar Bongo won an absolute majority in multi-party presidential elections, retaining the post he held for 26 years,
1993 - U.S. astronauts finished a gruelling five-day repair work on the $3 billion Hubble Space Telescope.
1994 - Britain and Sinn Fein, the Irish Republican Army's political wing, held their first formal talks for more than 70 years.

1995 - Poland's Supreme Court confirmed the victory of ex-communist Aleksander Kwasniewski in November's presidential election, rejecting turning down protests from supporters of defeated former Solidarity hero Lech Walesa.
